title: Ordered JSON field tolerance and repair workflow for quantized inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As we roll out FP8 and INT8 profiles for a subset of open models, we've observed rare but repeatable structured-output failures that standard schema validators miss. Symptoms include field ordering changes that downstream consumers treat as semantic errors, minor numeric truncation in typed fields, and occasional duplicate keys when tokenization boundaries shift under aggressive quantization. This ticket scopes a targeted tolerance and automated repair workflow that sits after model decoding but before final schema validation to improve practical function-calling reliability under low-bit inference.
goal: Reduce production parse-and-apply failures for function-calls under FP8/INT8 to <0.5% of invocations for canary workloads, and provide a safe automatic-repair pipeline that preserves semantics while surfacing ambiguous cases for human review.
acceptance_criteria: Canary run across 50k prompts shows parse_success >= 99.5% for INT8 profiles compared to baseline FP16 on same model family

Automated repair heuristics (field reordering, numeric re-casting, duplicate-key resolution) correctly fix >= 95% of parse failures on labeled validation set without changing semantic intent in manual audit (n=200)
Clear rollback triggers: if downstream application-level rejection rate increases by >0.3 percentage points after repair-enabled deploy, traffic auto-rolls back within configured window
Repair logs and diffs are persisted to Redact-safe storage and surfaced to Console with per-request deltas for debugging
test_plan: Assemble validation corpus: 40k real-product prompts + 10k synthetic edge cases (long arrays, nested objects, numeric edge ranges)
Run inference across model variants and quant profiles: FP16 baseline, FP8, INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric
Measure: parse_success, key_count_variation, field_order_distance (Levenshtein on key sequences), numeric_delta_stats (median, 95th percentile)
Evaluate automated repair module on subset and generate human audit labels for 200 repaired examples
Canary deploy repair pipeline behind feature flag for 10% of traffic in dedicated env with extended logging
progress_updates: 2025-02-05: Ticket created after incidents where downstream ingestion failed due to out-of-order object keys under INT8
2025-02-07: Spike implemented to measure field-order variance; initial metric shows 0.9% of responses had non-deterministic key ordering vs baseline
2025-02-10: Prototype repair library (reorder-by-schema + numeric-recast) landed in PR #5123, unit tests for canonicalization added
2025-02-12: Validation corpus assembled (50k prompts) and first end-to-end run scheduled for 2025-02-13
design_notes: Prefer non-destructive repairs: preserve original text and attach repaired payload as separate field to aid debugging

Repair heuristics are layered: 1) syntactic clean-up (unclosed braces), 2) duplicate-key resolution preferring non-null/prioritized fields, 3) key reordering using model-provided schema ordering metadata if available, 4) numeric re-casting with tolerance thresholds
Avoid heuristics that infer new semantic fields or drop required fields without human approval
implementation_plan: Add a repair stage to the structured-output pipeline between tokenizer-decoder and schema-assertion
Implement field-order distance metric and integrate into Console as a per-route signal
Instrument inference path to emit compact repair diffs and a boolean 'repaired' flag
Expose feature flag and canary config in Dedicated and Hosted for controlled rollout
review_feedback: PM (Lina Chen): prefer conservative defaults for repair in hosted API; expose opt-in via per-API key setting
Security (Jonas Hsu): ensure diff attachments are scrubbed for PII and stored with access controls
Design (Maya Ortiz): surface repaired vs original in Console request inspector with color-coded diffs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Repair rules could mask model regressions and delay root-cause fixes. Mitigation: require alerting when repair rate exceeds threshold and tie to regression ticketing
Risk: Numeric recasting might silently change business metrics. Mitigation: enforce numeric-change thresholds and require manual audit for high-value routes
Risk: Increased latency from repair stage. Mitigation: implement fast-path that only runs repair when schema-assertion fails
next_steps: Complete full-corpus inference runs for FP8/INT8 and collect baseline metrics (owner: Diego)
Iterate on repair heuristics from audit feedback and finalize default config (owner: Aisha)
Prepare canary rollout plan and dashboard widgets for Console (owner: Product)
Schedule security review for storage of repair diffs (owner: Security)
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on pragmatic, reversible fixes rather than model-level retraining or quantization pipeline changes
If repair stage reduces signal quality for downstream ML, we will add an option to route repaired payloads to a separate debug sink
